judgments.reason: The candidate is the PhysioNet Siena Scalp EEG Database record (Detti 2020), the original release of the same 14-patient data that this BIDS dataset curates.
Detti et al. 2020 (Processes) presents the new Siena scalp EEG database of 14 epileptic patients, the same data the BIDS README says is described in this paper.
judgments.paper_title: EEG Synchronization Analysis for Seizure Prediction: A Study on Data of Noninvasive Recordings

judgments.reason: Detti et al. 2018 is a seizure prediction method paper (EEG synchronization) that uses public scalp EEG; the dataset's described paper is Detti 2020 Processes, not this one.
judgments.paper_title: A Patient-Specific Approach for Short-Term Epileptic Seizures Prediction Through the Analysis of EEG Synchronization

judgments.reason: The paper describes PhysioNet as a data-sharing platform that hosts the source release; it is a platform paper, not this dataset's data paper.
judgments.paper_title: PhysioNet as a global platform for biomedical research

judgments.reason: Zenodo record is another deposit of the same Siena Scalp EEG data, a BIDS version of the Detti database; same data, though it keeps only 19 channels.
judgments.paper_venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

judgments.reason: SzCORE is an evaluation framework and benchmark for seizure detection algorithms that uses public datasets like Siena; it is a standard/method, not this dataset's data paper.
judgments.paper_title: SzCORE : Seizure Community Open‐Source Research Evaluation framework for the validation of electroencephalography ‐based automated seizure detection algorithms
